# The Houses That Remember: Discover Eight Remarkable Lives on the French Riviera


**Beautiful houses. Extraordinary lives. Stories that outlasted them both.** The French Riviera is full of remarkable houses. Some stand behind elaborate garden gates. Others overlook the Mediterranean from rocky cliffs. A few are former luxury hotels, transformed into private apartments long after their famous residents departed. It's easy to admire the buildings. But what happened inside them? Who chose to live there, and why? Who worked, struggled, collected art, designed furniture or planted gardens? What happened when those people could no longer maintain the lives they had created?

These questions are at the heart of **The Houses That Remember: Eight True Stories of Remarkable Lives on the French Riviera**, the new book by Anton Biletskyi-Volokh, published in 2026 as part of the AzurBooks series. Beginning in Menton and continuing west towards Nice, the book explores eight real places through the lives of the people associated with them. Among its subjects are Katherine Mansfield, Eileen Gray, Ferdinand Bac, Béatrice Ephrussi de Rothschild, Théodore Reinach and Henri Matisse. But the stories are about more than famous names.

They're about friendships, illness, money, artistic ambition, domestic life and the complicated question of what it means to preserve a home after its inhabitants are gone. This companion guide takes you to the places behind the book. Some can be visited inside. Others offer beautiful gardens or guided tours. A few remain private, making their history more accessible than their interiors. You don't have to read the book before following these routes. And if you have read it, this guide won't reveal the most important discoveries of each chapter.

Instead, it offers a new way to explore the French Riviera: **one house, one life and one question at a time.**

# The Houses That Remember : huit vies remarquables sur la Côte d'Azur

**De belles maisons. Des vies extraordinaires. Des histoires qui leur ont survécu.** La Côte d'Azur regorge de demeures remarquables. Certaines se cachent derrière des grilles de jardins ouvragées ; d'autres dominent la Méditerranée depuis des falaises. D'anciens hôtels de luxe sont devenus des appartements privés après le départ de leurs célèbres résidents. On admire facilement les bâtiments. Mais que s'y passait-il ? Qui a choisi d'y vivre, de travailler, de collectionner, de dessiner des meubles ou de planter des jardins ? Qu'est-il arrivé lorsque ces personnes n'ont plus pu maintenir le monde qu'elles avaient créé ?

Ces questions traversent **The Houses That Remember: Eight True Stories of Remarkable Lives on the French Riviera**, le nouveau livre d'Anton Biletskyi-Volokh, publié en anglais en 2026 dans la collection AzurBooks. De Menton vers Nice, il explore huit lieux réels à travers leurs habitants : Katherine Mansfield, Eileen Gray, Ferdinand Bac, Béatrice Ephrussi de Rothschild, Théodore Reinach et Henri Matisse notamment. Il ne s'agit pourtant pas seulement de noms célèbres, mais aussi d'amitié, de maladie, d'argent, d'ambition artistique et de vie domestique. Que signifie préserver une maison après la disparition de ses occupants ?

Ce guide vous conduit vers les lieux du livre. Certains proposent une visite intérieure, d'autres des jardins ou des visites accompagnées ; quelques-uns restent privés. On peut suivre ces parcours sans avoir lu le livre. Les lecteurs n'y trouveront pas les révélations essentielles de chaque chapitre, mais une autre manière d'explorer la Riviera : **une maison, une vie et une question à la fois.**

# The Houses That Remember: otto vite straordinarie sulla Costa Azzurra

**Case bellissime. Vite straordinarie. Storie sopravvissute a entrambe.** La Riviera francese è piena di dimore notevoli: dietro cancelli di giardini elaborati, sulle scogliere mediterranee, negli antichi alberghi di lusso diventati appartamenti privati dopo la partenza degli ospiti famosi. Ammirare gli edifici è facile. Ma cosa accadeva al loro interno? Chi scelse di abitarvi e perché? Chi lavorava, lottava, collezionava arte, disegnava mobili o piantava giardini? E cosa successe quando non fu più possibile mantenere quel mondo?

Sono le domande di **The Houses That Remember: Eight True Stories of Remarkable Lives on the French Riviera**, il nuovo libro di Anton Biletskyi-Volokh, pubblicato in inglese nel 2026 nella serie AzurBooks. Da Mentone verso Nizza, racconta otto luoghi reali attraverso le persone che li abitarono: Katherine Mansfield, Eileen Gray, Ferdinand Bac, Béatrice Ephrussi de Rothschild, Théodore Reinach e Henri Matisse, fra gli altri. Non sono soltanto biografie celebri: sono amicizia, malattia, denaro, ambizione artistica, vita domestica e la difficile scelta di conservare una casa quando i suoi abitanti non ci sono più.

# The Houses That Remember: вісім незвичайних життів на Французькій Рив'єрі

**Прекрасні будинки. Незвичайні життя. Історії, що пережили і ті, й інші.** На Французькій Рив'єрі чимало особливих осель: за вишуканими садовими брамами, на скелях над Середземним морем, у колишніх розкішних готелях, які давно стали приватними квартирами. Будівлями легко милуватися. Але що відбувалося всередині? Хто оселився тут і чому? Хто працював, боровся, збирав мистецтво, проєктував меблі чи садив сади? Що сталося, коли люди вже не могли підтримувати створений ними світ?

Ці запитання лежать в основі **The Houses That Remember: Eight True Stories of Remarkable Lives on the French Riviera**, нової книги Антона Білецького-Волоха, виданої англійською 2026 року в серії AzurBooks. Від Ментона на захід до Ніцци вона досліджує вісім реальних місць через пов'язані з ними життя: Кетрін Менсфілд, Ейлін Ґрей, Фердинанда Бака, Беатріс Ефруссі де Ротшильд, Теодора Рейнаха й Анрі Матісса та інших. Це не просто відомі імена, а дружба, хвороби, гроші, творчі прагнення, побут і складне питання: як зберегти дім після зникнення його мешканців?

Цей супровідний гід веде до місць із книги. Десь можна побувати всередині, десь відвідати сад або екскурсію, інші оселі залишаються приватними. Читати книгу перед прогулянкою необов'язково. Для читачів тут немає головних відкриттів кожного розділу, натомість є інший спосіб знайомства з Рив'єрою: **один будинок, одне життя й одне запитання за раз.**

## 1. Villa Isola Bella, Menton: the room that wasn't hers

**The person:** Katherine Mansfield

**The story:** _A Room at Isola Bella_

In September 1920, Katherine Mansfield returned to Menton. She was thirty-one, seriously ill with tuberculosis and searching for conditions that would allow her to continue writing. At Villa Isola Bella, in the Garavan district, she found a place surrounded by the subtropical vegetation and Mediterranean light that made Menton such an attractive winter destination. But the most interesting part of the story isn't simply that a famous writer stayed here. It's the question of what later generations choose to preserve.

A room associated with Mansfield eventually became a memorial and a working space for visiting New Zealand writers. Yet that memorial room wasn't the room in which Mansfield had written. The original evidence takes us elsewhere: to surviving letters, manuscripts, photographs and the people who shared her daily life. One of them was Ida Baker, whose practical and personal support forms an important part of the book's account.

### Why visit this area?

Garavan offers an opportunity to understand Menton's history as an international winter retreat. Its villas, gardens, hillside setting and relationship with the sea help explain why writers and other visitors came here long before modern beach tourism.

### Can you visit the house?

Villa Isola Bella should not be treated as an ordinary walk-in museum. The historic address is associated with private and restricted premises. We couldn't establish a dependable current public visiting programme for independent tourists. Don't enter the grounds, approach residential doors or assume a commemorative association permits access.

### A good alternative

Explore the public streets of Garavan and visit another garden connected with the book, Val Rahmeh, when open.

**What the book adds:** The distinction between a place as it was lived in and the memorial created afterwards.

## 1. Villa Isola Bella, Menton : la chambre qui n'était pas la sienne

**La personne :** Katherine Mansfield. **Le récit :** _A Room at Isola Bella_.

En septembre 1920, Katherine Mansfield revient à Menton. Elle a trente et un ans, souffre gravement de tuberculose et cherche des conditions lui permettant de continuer à écrire. À la Villa Isola Bella, dans le quartier de Garavan, elle trouve cette végétation subtropicale et cette lumière méditerranéenne qui attiraient les hivernants.

L'histoire ne se limite pas au séjour d'une écrivaine célèbre : elle interroge ce que les générations suivantes décident de conserver. Une chambre associée à Mansfield devient un lieu de mémoire et de travail pour des écrivains néo-zélandais. Pourtant, ce n'est pas la chambre dans laquelle elle écrivait. Les lettres, manuscrits, photographies et témoignages de ses proches conduisent ailleurs. Ida Baker, dont le soutien quotidien et personnel compte dans le récit, fait partie de ces présences essentielles.

### Pourquoi découvrir ce quartier ?

Les villas, jardins, pentes et vues maritimes de Garavan éclairent l'histoire de Menton comme refuge hivernal international. Ils expliquent pourquoi des écrivains venaient ici bien avant le tourisme balnéaire moderne.

### Peut-on visiter la maison ?

Ne considérez pas Isola Bella comme un musée ouvert sans rendez-vous. Les locaux sont privés ou soumis à des restrictions ; aucun programme public régulier et fiable n'a été confirmé pour les voyageurs indépendants. N'entrez pas dans la propriété, n'approchez pas les portes des logements et ne supposez pas qu'un souvenir littéraire autorise l'accès.

### Une bonne alternative

Promenez-vous dans les rues publiques de Garavan, puis visitez Val Rahmeh lorsqu'il est ouvert. **L'apport du livre :** distinguer le lieu vécu du mémorial construit après coup.

## 1. Villa Isola Bella, Mentone: la stanza che non era la sua

**La persona:** Katherine Mansfield. **Il racconto:** _A Room at Isola Bella_.

Nel settembre 1920 Katherine Mansfield torna a Mentone. Ha trentun anni, è gravemente malata di tubercolosi e cerca condizioni che le permettano di continuare a scrivere. A Villa Isola Bella, nel quartiere di Garavan, trova vegetazione subtropicale e luce mediterranea: le stesse ragioni che avevano reso Mentone una destinazione invernale internazionale.

La storia non riguarda soltanto il soggiorno di una scrittrice famosa, ma ciò che le generazioni successive scelgono di conservare. Una stanza legata a Mansfield diventa un memoriale e un luogo di lavoro per scrittori neozelandesi. Eppure non è la stanza dove aveva scritto. Lettere, manoscritti, fotografie e persone che condividevano la sua quotidianità conducono altrove. Fra queste c'è Ida Baker, il cui sostegno pratico e personale è essenziale nel racconto.

### Perché esplorare questa zona?

Ville, giardini, colline e rapporto con il mare aiutano a comprendere Mentone come rifugio invernale internazionale, frequentato da scrittori molto prima del moderno turismo balneare.

### Si può entrare nella casa?

Non trattate Isola Bella come un museo aperto senza appuntamento. Si tratta di locali privati o soggetti a restrizioni; non è stato verificato un programma pubblico regolare e affidabile per visitatori indipendenti. Non entrate nei terreni, non avvicinate le porte delle abitazioni e non considerate un legame commemorativo come permesso d'accesso.

### Un'alternativa utile

Passeggiate nelle strade pubbliche di Garavan e visitate Val Rahmeh quando è aperto. **Cosa aggiunge il libro:** la distinzione fra un luogo vissuto e il memoriale creato dopo.

## 1. Villa Isola Bella, Ментон: кімната, що була не її

**Людина:** Кетрін Менсфілд. **Історія:** _A Room at Isola Bella_.

У вересні 1920 року Кетрін Менсфілд повернулася до Ментона. Їй тридцять один, вона тяжко хвора на туберкульоз і шукає умов, які дозволять продовжувати писати. На Villa Isola Bella в Гаравані вона знаходить субтропічну рослинність і середземноморське світло, що зробили Ментон популярним зимовим прихистком.

Найцікавіше тут не просто перебування відомої письменниці, а те, що вирішують зберігати наступні покоління. Пов'язана з Менсфілд кімната стала меморіалом і робочим простором для новозеландських письменників. Проте це не та кімната, де вона писала. Листи, рукописи, фотографії та люди, які ділили її побут, ведуть до іншого місця. Серед них Іда Бейкер: її практична й особиста підтримка посідає важливе місце в книжковій розповіді.

### Навіщо гуляти цим районом?

Вілли, сади, схили й близькість моря допомагають зрозуміти Ментон як міжнародний зимовий курорт. Письменники приїжджали сюди задовго до сучасного пляжного туризму.

### Чи можна зайти в будинок?

Не сприймайте Isola Bella як музей із вільним входом. Приміщення приватні або обмежені в доступі; надійну регулярну програму для самостійних туристів не підтверджено. Не заходьте на територію, не підходьте до житлових дверей і не вважайте меморіальний зв'язок дозволом на відвідування.

### Хороша альтернатива

Пройдіться громадськими вулицями Гаравана й відвідайте Val Rahmeh, коли сад відкритий. **Що додає книга:** різницю між місцем, де людина жила, та меморіалом, створеним згодом.

## 2. Val Rahmeh: the garden that outgrew the house

**Location:** Avenue Saint-Jacques, Menton

**The person:** Maybud Sherwood Campbell

**The story:** _The Garden That Outgrew the House_

Val Rahmeh is one of Menton's most remarkable botanical gardens. Today, it's managed by France's National Museum of Natural History and contains an extraordinary collection of tropical, subtropical and Mediterranean plants. But its existence is closely connected with a woman whose ambitions eventually exceeded her financial resources. Maybud Sherwood Campbell acquired the property in 1957. A former opera singer with serious botanical interests, she enlarged the plant collection and transformed the garden. ## 4. E-1027: a modern house that raises difficult questions

On a rocky stretch of coastline west of Menton stands a small white modernist villa. Its name is E-1027. Designed by Eileen Gray in collaboration with Jean Badovici, the house is one of the most important examples of early modernist domestic architecture. It looks deceptively simple. White walls, slender supports, large openings and terraces overlooking the sea. But almost every detail was carefully considered. Windows, shutters, furniture and room arrangements were intended to respond to the needs of the people living inside.

The book begins with something particularly revealing: a window mechanism designed to manage light, ventilation and privacy. What sounds like a minor architectural detail becomes an introduction to much larger questions. Who designs a home? Who gets credit for it? And what happens when later interventions change the character of a carefully conceived interior?

### Why is this place worth visiting?

E-1027 is more than a beautiful house. It's an opportunity to understand architecture as a collection of decisions about daily life. A window isn't merely a decorative opening. A chair isn't simply furniture. The entire space is designed around movement, comfort and relationships between people and their surroundings.

### Visiting information

E-1027 forms part of the Cap Moderne heritage site. For the published 2026 season, visits operate from April through October, with guided tours and mandatory online reservations. The standard individual ticket is listed at €18. The published season ends on 31 October 2026; later visits require a newly confirmed programme. The meeting point is associated with Roquebrune-Cap-Martin railway station. Access includes a pedestrian approach and uneven ground with stairs. Some sections may be restricted because of conservation work.

## 6. Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild: the woman who built a world

**Location:** Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat

**The person:** Béatrice Ephrussi de Rothschild

**The story:** _The Woman Who Built a World_

Few houses on the French Riviera are as visually spectacular as Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild. Its elegant pink façades, richly decorated rooms and elaborate gardens seem almost designed for a dream of aristocratic Riviera life. The villa was created for Béatrice Ephrussi de Rothschild, a collector with extraordinary resources and very definite ideas about how her surroundings should look. One story associated with the garden's creation describes employees moving cardboard representations of trees so that Béatrice could judge the appearance of different arrangements.

The book treats this as a historical anecdote rather than presenting every detail as independently documented. The larger story, however, is unmistakable. Béatrice created an environment in which architecture, decoration, gardens and collections were brought together according to her personal tastes.

### What should you see?

The interiors offer a glimpse of the world she assembled. Outside, the themed gardens provide a journey through different landscape traditions. The formal French garden, exotic planting and other carefully composed spaces are attractions in their own right.

### Visiting information

Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild is a public museum and garden. It operates year-round under published seasonal hours, with occasional exceptional closures. During the winter period from November 2026 to January 2027, the official schedule lists shorter weekday hours and longer opening on weekends and school holidays. The villa's official website should be checked for current ticket prices, special events and visitor access conditions. It also announces an exceptional closure on 14 December 2026.

**Official website:** [Official website](https://villa-ephrussi.com/en/)

**What the book adds:** The decisions, personal ambition and eventual legacy behind one of the Riviera's most impressive private collections.

## 7. Villa Kérylos: an ancient dream with modern plumbing

**Location:** Rue Gustave Eiffel, Beaulieu-sur-Mer

**The people:** Théodore and Fanny Reinach, architect Emmanuel Pontremoli

**The story:** _An Ancient Dream with Modern Plumbing_

What happens when someone decides to build an ancient Greek house in the twentieth century? At Villa Kérylos, the answer is fascinating. Théodore Reinach was a scholar with a deep interest in classical Greece. With architect Emmanuel Pontremoli, he created a villa inspired by the architecture, decorative arts and domestic life of antiquity. Yet the family was living in the modern world. They needed functioning bathrooms, comfortable rooms and contemporary conveniences. One particularly delightful example concerns Fanny Reinach's piano. An ordinary piano hardly belonged in a carefully constructed ancient Greek interior.

So the instrument was concealed within a specially designed cabinet, allowing modern music-making to coexist with the historical concept of the house.

### What makes Kérylos special?

Unlike a museum displaying ancient objects in ordinary rooms, Kérylos attempts to recreate an entire domestic environment. You can explore architectural details, mosaics, painted decoration, furniture and the relationship between the villa and its coastal setting. It's a wonderful place to consider how people imagine the past.

### Visiting information

Villa Kérylos is normally open to the public. The current official schedule lists 10 a.m.–5 p.m. from October to March and 10 a.m.–6 p.m. from April to September. Standard adult admission is listed at €15. The villa's website states that regular tickets are sold on site rather than through external online ticket platforms.

**Important:** Due to works, Rue Gustave Eiffel has pedestrian-only access. Check the approach if you have mobility limitations.

The site also has specific restrictions concerning pushchairs and pets.

**Official website:** [Official website](https://www.villakerylos.fr/)

**What the book adds:** The tension between historical authenticity and the needs of a family living in the twentieth century.

**The person:** Henri Matisse

**The story:** _The Hotel That Became a Studio_

The final chapter of _The Houses That Remember_ takes us to Nice. Here, in the former Hôtel Régina, Henri Matisse lived and worked during an extraordinary period of his artistic life. The building had once been a grand hotel associated with the fashionable Belle Époque resort of Nice. By the time Matisse lived there, it had become a residential building. Its spacious rooms gave the artist an environment in which he could develop some of his most ambitious later compositions. One especially memorable work was _The Swimming Pool_, created in 1952.

Using shapes cut from painted paper, Matisse transformed the walls of a room into a world of swimmers, divers and sea creatures. The work was connected to the specific room in which it was made. Yet preserving it would eventually require separating the composition from that original setting.

### Can you visit Matisse's apartment?

No ordinary public interior access is available. Le Régina is a residential property, not the Musée Matisse. Its façade can be appreciated from public areas, but the building's private entrances, gardens and apartments must be respected.

### Where should you go instead?

Visit the **Musée Matisse Nice**, also in Cimiez. The museum explores Matisse's artistic development and his long relationship with Nice. The surrounding Cimiez district is also worth exploring for its Belle Époque architecture, gardens and cultural heritage. The museum is a separate institution rather than Matisse's preserved private apartment.

**Official museum:** [Official website](https://www.musee-matisse-nice.org/)

**What the book adds:** The relationship between an artist's working space, the work created there and the difficult decisions involved in preservation.

## Three ways to explore the houses from Menton

Trying to visit all eight properties in one day would turn a fascinating cultural journey into a rushed transport exercise. A better approach is to choose the route that suits your interests and the time available.

### Route A. A day in Menton: writers, gardens and extraordinary lives

Begin with a visit to Val Rahmeh, when the garden is open. Explore Garavan's historic surroundings, remembering that Villa Isola Bella is not a confirmed public museum. If you have arranged a guided visit to Fontana Rosa, plan the day's timing around its reservation. Les Colombières is a further possibility for a separate, confirmed guided tour. However, its uphill location and restricted access make it unsuitable as a spontaneous addition.

**Recommended approach:** Choose Val Rahmeh plus one organised historic garden, rather than attempting all four sites.

**Allow:** A full day with breaks, or two half-days if you prefer a slower pace.

### Route B. Modernism and Mediterranean architecture

Choose a date when E-1027 has a confirmed guided tour. Travel from Menton to Roquebrune-Cap-Martin and follow the operator's instructions for reaching Cap Moderne. Allow time for the guided visit, including the pedestrian approach. Afterwards, enjoy the coastline or return to Menton. You could add another nearby location on a different day, but the E-1027 tour deserves time on its own.

**Allow:** Approximately half a day, including transport.

### Route C. The collectors and artists: a longer Riviera experience

Visit Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild in Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat. On a separate excursion, discover Villa Kérylos in Beaulieu-sur-Mer. Continue to Nice on another day for the Matisse Museum and an exterior view of Le Régina in Cimiez. This provides an opportunity to explore three very different interpretations of what a house can become: a collector's world, a reconstruction of antiquity and an artist's working environment.

**Allow:** Two relaxed days for the three main cultural visits, or longer if you enjoy gardens and museums.

## Три способи дослідити будинки з Ментона

Так можна зіставити три різні перетворення оселі: світ колекціонерки, реконструкцію античності й робоче середовище художника. **Час:** щонайменше два неспішні дні для трьох основних культурних відвідувань або більше, якщо любите музеї й сади.

## What the houses can't tell us

A beautifully restored house can create a powerful illusion. It may seem as though the people who lived there have only just stepped outside. Their furniture is arranged. Their books are displayed. Their gardens are maintained. Yet the past is never quite that easy to reconstruct. The book examines the difference between documented history and the stories later generations tell about it. A memorial room may not be the room where someone worked. A garden can survive while changing so dramatically that its creator would barely recognise it.

A building's restoration may preserve some aspects of its history while altering others. And the people who supported a celebrated writer or artist may be almost invisible in the surviving public story. This is why the eight houses are worth visiting, even if you've never opened the book. They encourage a different kind of attention. Rather than asking only, “Who lived here?”, you might ask, “Who made it possible for them to live and work here?”

And rather than seeing restoration as the end of the story, you may begin to see it as another chapter.

## Ce que les maisons ne peuvent pas nous dire

Une maison restaurée donne parfois l'impression que ses habitants viennent de sortir. Meubles disposés, livres exposés, jardins entretenus : pourtant, reconstruire le passé n'est jamais si simple. Le livre distingue l'histoire documentée des récits des générations suivantes.

Une chambre mémorielle n'est pas forcément celle où l'on travaillait. Un jardin peut survivre tout en devenant méconnaissable pour son créateur. Restaurer peut préserver certains éléments et en modifier d'autres. Les personnes qui soutenaient un artiste ou un écrivain deviennent parfois presque invisibles dans le récit public.

Voilà pourquoi ces lieux valent une visite même sans avoir lu le livre. Ils invitent à demander non seulement « Qui vivait ici ? », mais « Qui lui a permis d'y vivre et d'y travailler ? ». La restauration n'est alors plus la fin de l'histoire, mais un nouveau chapitre.

## Quello che le case non possono raccontare

Una casa restaurata può far pensare che gli abitanti siano appena usciti: mobili disposti, libri esposti, giardini curati. Ricostruire il passato, però, non è così semplice. Il libro distingue la storia documentata dai racconti delle generazioni successive.

La stanza commemorativa può non essere quella del lavoro. Un giardino sopravvive cambiando fino a diventare irriconoscibile per il suo autore. Un restauro conserva alcuni aspetti e ne modifica altri. Chi sosteneva uno scrittore o un artista può quasi sparire dalla storia pubblica.

È una ragione per visitare questi luoghi anche senza aver letto il libro. Oltre a «Chi viveva qui?», chiedetevi «Chi gli permetteva di vivere e lavorare qui?». Il restauro non sarà più la fine della storia, ma un altro capitolo.

## Чого будинки не можуть розповісти

Реставрований дім може створити ілюзію, ніби мешканці щойно вийшли: меблі розставлено, книжки виставлено, сад доглянуто. Та відновити минуле не так просто. Книга розглядає різницю між документованою історією та розповідями пізніших поколінь.

Меморіальна кімната може виявитися не тією, де працювали. Сад переживає творця, але змінюється до невпізнаваності. Реставрація зберігає одне й перетворює інше. Люди, які підтримували відомого автора чи художника, іноді майже зникають із публічного наративу.

Саме тому ці місця цікаві й без читання книги. Крім «Хто тут жив?», варто запитати «Хто дозволяв йому тут жити й працювати?». Тоді реставрація постане не завершенням, а наступним розділом історії.

## Practical questions before visiting

### Do I need to book every house?

No. Some, such as Villa Kérylos and Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild, offer ordinary public admission. Others, including E-1027, Fontana Rosa and Les Colombières, require advance arrangements or guided visits. Villa Isola Bella and Le Régina shouldn't be treated as ordinary public attractions.

### Can I visit all eight houses without a car?

Several locations can be reached using regional trains and local transport, but not every final approach is convenient. Some properties are uphill, have limited bus service or require substantial walking. For Les Colombières and other restricted estates, organise the visit and access separately.

### Is the route suitable for wheelchair users?

Not as one continuous accessible itinerary. Several historic gardens and villas contain stairs, uneven paths or steep approaches. Check accessibility directly with each operator before booking.

### Is this guide a substitute for the book?

No. The guide introduces the people and places and provides contemporary visitor information. The book tells their stories in depth, drawing on historical evidence, correspondence and published research. You can enjoy either independently.

### Is the book fiction?

No. _The Houses That Remember_ is narrative nonfiction. It examines eight real historical places and the lives of people associated with them, while acknowledging uncertainty where sources are incomplete or contradictory.

## Questions pratiques avant la visite

### Faut-il tout réserver ?

Non. Kérylos et Ephrussi proposent une entrée publique ordinaire. E-1027, Fontana Rosa et Les Colombières demandent réservation ou visite guidée. Isola Bella et Le Régina ne sont pas des attractions librement accessibles.

### Peut-on voir les huit lieux sans voiture ?

Plusieurs sont accessibles en train régional et transports locaux, mais le dernier tronçon n'est pas toujours pratique : pentes, desserte limitée ou marche importante. Pour les propriétés privées, organisez séparément visite et accès.

### Est-ce accessible en fauteuil roulant ?

Pas comme itinéraire continu garanti. Jardins et villas historiques comportent marches, chemins irréguliers et pentes. Vérifiez directement avec chaque exploitant avant de réserver.

### Le guide remplace-t-il le livre ?

Non. Il présente les personnes, les lieux et les conditions actuelles de visite. Le livre approfondit leurs histoires à partir de correspondances, sources historiques et recherches publiées. Les deux se lisent indépendamment.

### Est-ce un roman ?

Non : _The Houses That Remember_ est un récit de non-fiction. Il examine huit lieux réels et leurs habitants en signalant les incertitudes lorsque les sources sont lacunaires ou contradictoires.

## Domande pratiche prima di partire

No. Kérylos ed Ephrussi offrono ingresso pubblico ordinario. E-1027, Fontana Rosa e Les Colombières richiedono prenotazioni o visite accompagnate. Isola Bella e Le Régina non sono normali attrazioni liberamente visitabili.

### Si possono raggiungere tutte senza auto?

Diversi luoghi sono accessibili con treni regionali e trasporti locali, ma l'ultimo tratto non è sempre comodo: salite, servizi limitati o camminate importanti. Per tenute private organizzate separatamente visita e accesso.

### È un itinerario adatto alle sedie a rotelle?

Non come percorso continuo garantito. Giardini e ville storiche presentano scale, fondi irregolari e pendenze. Chiedete direttamente a ogni gestore prima di prenotare.

### La guida sostituisce il libro?

No. Introduce persone, luoghi e informazioni attuali per visitarli. Il libro approfondisce le storie attraverso fonti, lettere e ricerche pubblicate. Entrambi si possono apprezzare indipendentemente.

### È narrativa di finzione?

No. _The Houses That Remember_ è saggistica narrativa: esamina otto luoghi storici reali e i loro abitanti, segnalando le incertezze delle fonti incomplete o contraddittorie.

## Практичні запитання перед відвідуванням

### Чи скрізь потрібне бронювання?

Ні. Kérylos та Ephrussi пропонують звичайний публічний вхід. E-1027, Fontana Rosa й Les Colombières потребують запису чи екскурсії. Isola Bella та Le Régina не є звичайними відкритими пам'ятками.

### Чи можна обійтися без автомобіля?

До кількох місць можна доїхати регіональним потягом і місцевим транспортом, але остання ділянка не завжди зручна: підйоми, рідкі автобуси чи довга хода. Для приватних маєтків окремо організуйте відвідування та підхід.

### Чи підходить маршрут для крісел колісних?

Не як єдиний гарантовано доступний маршрут. В історичних садах і віллах є сходи, нерівні доріжки та круті підходи. Перед бронюванням уточніть умови безпосередньо в кожного оператора.

### Чи замінює гід книгу?

Ні. Він знайомить із людьми, місцями й поточними умовами відвідування. Книга детально розповідає історії на основі джерел, листування та опублікованих досліджень. Обидва тексти можна читати незалежно.

### Це художня вигадка?

Ні. _The Houses That Remember_ — наративний нонфікшн про вісім реальних історичних місць і пов'язаних із ними людей. Неповні або суперечливі джерела позначені як невизначені.

## Read the stories, then visit the places

A house can preserve a view, a staircase, a garden or a room. It cannot preserve an entire life. That's what makes the stories behind these eight places so fascinating. Katherine Mansfield, Maybud Campbell, Vicente Blasco Ibáñez, Eileen Gray, Ferdinand Bac, Béatrice Ephrussi de Rothschild, Théodore Reinach and Henri Matisse all wanted something from the places they inhabited. Some wanted somewhere to work. Some wanted to create an ideal home. Some wanted to gather objects, preserve beauty or experiment with new ways of living. The buildings remain, but their meanings have changed.

_The Houses That Remember_ invites you to explore those changes through the people who experienced them. And this guide offers a way to visit the places yourself, without confusing the beauty of a building with the full complexity of its history. Whether you visit one garden in Menton or spend several days travelling west towards Nice, you may find yourself looking at the Riviera differently. Not just admiring its houses. Wondering what they remember.

## Leggere le storie, poi visitare i luoghi

Una casa conserva un panorama, una scala, un giardino o una stanza, non un'intera vita. Katherine Mansfield, Maybud Campbell, Vicente Blasco Ibáñez, Eileen Gray, Ferdinand Bac, Béatrice Ephrussi de Rothschild, Théodore Reinach e Henri Matisse cercavano qualcosa nelle proprie abitazioni: lavorare, creare una casa ideale, raccogliere oggetti, preservare bellezza o sperimentare modi di vivere.

La guida aiuta a vedere i luoghi senza confonderne la bellezza con l'intera complessità storica. Un giardino a Mentone o più giorni verso Nizza possono cambiare lo sguardo: non soltanto ammirare le case, ma chiedersi cosa ricordino.

## Прочитати історії, а потім побачити місця

Дім може зберегти краєвид, сходи, сад чи кімнату, але не ціле життя. Кетрін Менсфілд, Мейбад Кемпбелл, Вісенте Бласко Ібаньєс, Ейлін Ґрей, Фердинанд Бак, Беатріс Ефруссі де Ротшильд, Теодор Рейнах та Анрі Матісс чогось шукали у своїх оселях: можливості працювати, створити ідеальний дім, збирати речі, зберігати красу чи випробувати інший спосіб життя.

Будівлі залишилися, а їхні значення змінилися. Книга досліджує ці зміни через тих, хто їх пережив. Гід дозволяє відвідати місця, не плутаючи красу з усією складністю історії. Один сад у Ментоні чи кілька днів дорогою до Ніцци можуть змінити погляд: не просто милуватися будинками, а думати, що вони пам'ятають.
